title: Abramorama Acquires ‘Miss Represenation: Rise Up,’ Jennifer Siebel Newsom Documentary About Backlash Against Women In Social Media Age
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Points North Institute Announces 2026 Artist Programs And Points North Forum Ahead of Camden Film Festival Abramorama Acquires ‘Miss Represenation: Rise Up,’ Jennifer Siebel Newsom Documentary About Backlash Against Women In Social Media Age Kino Lorber Acquires ‘A Fox Under A Pink Moon,’ Oscar-Contending Doc That’s “A Diary, A Survival Story, An Artistic Manifesto” View All August 31, 2026 8:00am 'Miss Representation: Rise Up' Abramorama EXCLUSIVE: Abramorama has acquired North American distribution rights to Miss Representation: Rise Up , director Jennifer Siebel Newsom ’s examination of the “backlash against women in the age of AI, social media, and rising misogyny.” The company plans to premiere the film at IFC Center in New York City on October 22, before a rollout to theaters across North America. That will qualify the documentary for the Oscar race. Miss Representation: Rise Up , the follow-up to Newsom’s 2011 film Miss Representation , premiered in June at Tribeca Festival in New York. The new film “dives deep into the alarming mental health crisis affecting women’s agency and power,” notes a release. “With the proliferation of AI deepfakes and the online ‘manosphere,’ this new era of tech-facilitated violence is exacerbating sexism and misogyny towards women and girls in an attempt to objectify, control, and silence them. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Documentary 'The Work In Progress' Trailer: Documentary From E.P. Robert Reich Finds Potent Way To "Help Bridge America's Deepest Divides" Acquisitions Abramorama Takes NA Rights To 'Knife: The Attempted Murder Of Salman Rushdie,' Alex Gibney Film About Author Attacked By Islamic Fanatic Abramorama “Highlighting a new generation of inspiring young women who are actively pushing back, Miss Representation: Rise Up interweaves women’s personal journeys with insights from influential voices across politics, media, technology, advocacy, and academia, including Hillary Rodham Clinton, Nancy Pelosi, Amy Klobuchar, Safiya Noble, Frances Haugen, Reshma Saujani, Jameela Jamil, Gretchen Carlson, and Jim Steyer, to reimagine a future that finally uplifts women and girls.” We have your exclusive look at the film in the trailer below. “Jennifer Siebel Newsom has spent over a decade holding up a mirror to how our culture treats women,” said Karol Martesko-Fenster, CEO of AB2 Media Group and Abramorama, and Damon G. Smith, SVP of Creative Strategy and Business Growth. “This timely and incisive film documents a troubling crisis that no one – women, parents, educators, policy makers – can afford to ignore, and introduces us to the young women meeting it head-on. We’re proud to bring this vital, galvanizing work to theaters across North America.” Photo by Cheng Xin/Getty Images The acquisition comes following news of a $17.1 billion dollar settlement of a lawsuit brought by state attorneys general that accused Meta of designing its Facebook and Instagram platforms to addict young people and damage their mental health. Newsom’s film speaks directly to harm inflicted on young women who are routinely denigrated on social media and who face constant scrutiny of their appearance and comportment through online platforms. “We’re dealing with an aggressive predator of misogyny that’s coming at young women online,” actress/activist Jameela Jamil says in the trailer. Another expert reports, “We are putting young women through the most severe mental health crisis that the country has ever experienced.” Director Jennifer Siebel Newsom Courtesy of Andrew Paynter Newsom, who is California’s First Partner, executive produced the Emmy Award-winning and Oscar-nominated The Invisible War (2012), and the Emmy Award-winning documentaries The Hunting Ground (2015) and On the Record (2020). After releasing Miss Representation in 2011, she launched The Representation Project, “a nonprofit organization that uses film, media, and education as catalysts for cultural transformation.” “When I made my first documentary Miss Representation 15 years ago, I wanted my daughter and girls in her generation to use their voices and stand in their power as rightful leaders,” Newsom said in a statement. “Unfortunately, amidst progress for women and girls came extreme backlash. Technology is the newest and most powerful cultural communicator of our time – and it is being weaponized at an unprecedented scale to silence women and girls.” ‘Miss Representation: Rise Up’ Abramorama Newsom continued, “I hope Miss Representation: Rise Up continues to inspire women and girls to use their voice and stand in their power, just as I hope the film encourages boys and men to value women and girls and ensure we all have seats at decision-making tables. Abramorama understands the urgency of getting this story in front of as many people as possible. We are honored to partner with them.” Abramorama and The Representation Project present Miss Representation: Rise Up . Executive producers: Melinda French Gates & Pivotal, Melony & Adam Lewis, Aileen Getty Foundation, Susie Thompkins Buell, Harnisch Foundation, Minderoo Pictures, Jackie Zehner, Maureen Pelton & Charlie Hartwell, Patricia Arquette, Hadley Mullin, Emily Liu Foy, Brenda Robinson, and Barbara Bridges. Original music by Laura Karpman, with cinematography by Mario Furloni. Jessica Congdon and Jennifer Steinman Sternin edited the film. Miss Representation: Rise Up is written and produced by Camille Servan-Schreiber, Gretchen Miller, and Jennifer Siebel Newsom. title: Points North Institute Announces 2026 Artist Programs And Points North Forum Ahead of Camden Film Festival
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Points North Institute Announces 2026 Artist Programs And Points North Forum Ahead of Camden Film Festival Abramorama Acquires ‘Miss Represenation: Rise Up,’ Jennifer Siebel Newsom Documentary About Backlash Against Women In Social Media Age Kino Lorber Acquires ‘A Fox Under A Pink Moon,’ Oscar-Contending Doc That’s “A Diary, A Survival Story, An Artistic Manifesto” View All August 31, 2026 8:00am Documentary filmmakers set for the 2026 Points North Institute Artist Programs Points North Institute EXCLUSIVE: Documentary artists confronting media consolidation, a tightened acquisition market and other challenges are about to get a major lift from the Points North Institute , the nonprofit that puts on the Camden International Film Festival in Maine. On Monday, the institute announced its 2026 Artist Programs, a slate of pitching events, residencies, curated meetings and more that will support talented artists from diverse backgrounds. Prominent mentors, funders, and collaborators will be on hand to work with 40 teams across 27 countries who have documentary projects in development. “Three-quarters of the supported projects are directed or co-directed by filmmakers of color and 60% by women or non-binary filmmakers,” the institute said. Related Stories Documentary 22nd Camden Film Festival To Showcase New Work By Documentary's Leading Lights: Gibney, Kopple, Oppenheimer, Chin, Vasarhelyi, Poitras & More Documentary Ellis-Beauregard Foundation And Points North Institute Announce Major New Award For Documentary Filmmakers PNI also announced details of its annual Points North Forum that “will gather filmmakers and industry leaders for intimate, forward-looking conversations at a moment of profound change.” Several Forum sessions will address the state of public media, which saw deep funding cuts last year pushed by Pres. Trump and passed by the Republican-controlled Congress. Watch on Deadline Both the Artist Programs and the Points North Forum run in tandem with the Camden International Film Festival, set to unfold from Sept. 17-20 in the bucolic towns of Camden and Rockland in Maine’s mid-coast region. Scroll for details on the Artist Programs and Forum. “When so much of the infrastructure that has historically served independent filmmakers is being dismantled,” observed Sean Flynn , artistic director and co-founder of the Points North Institute, “it is more important than ever to create spaces where artists can find the time, resources, and community they need to bring their visions to life. It is an honor to support their journeys and convene the field to imagine and build more durable, abundant systems that will expand the horizons of the documentary form.” Artist Programs Highlights —The 17th annual Points North Pitch , part of the Points North Fellowship and one of North America’s leading documentary pitching forums, will see six feature docs in progress pitching to a panel of funders, producers and executives. Selected filmmakers will be mentored by Sundance Institute ’s Kristin Feeley and program alum Assia Boundaoui . —The second cohort of Diane Weyermann Fellows will gather for their final creative retreat. The program supports three director-producer teams with $100,000 unrestricted grants – one of the largest funds in the US – and an 18-month collaborative fellowship. Advisors include Tabitha Jackson , Kirsten Johnson and Andrea Meditch . —Additional programs include the LEF/CIFF Fellowship , supporting New England-based filmmakers working on feature documentaries, and the year-long 4th World Media Lab, which supports early- and mid-career Indigenous filmmakers from across Turtle Island, in partnership with Big Sky Documentary Festival and Seattle International Film Festival . —Points North will host cohorts from the BAVC MediaMaker Fellowship , CAAM’s Building Bridges Grantees, and the Disabled Nonfiction Producer Apprenticeship run by FWD-DOC and Multitude Films. The festival will serve as the kickoff for the second cycle of a collaboration between American Documentary | POV, Chicken & Egg Films, TIME Studios and Bird Street Productions focused on short documentaries. This cycle’s cohort includes Sierra Ulrich ( Dad Hair ) , Kristine Stolakis ( Hard Labor ), and Alyse Shorland ( Write Me a Letter ) . —Filmmakers will have access to 400+ curated meetings with more than 100 industry professionals through Points North’s 1:1 Meetings , including representatives from Sundance Institute, Hulu, Watermelon Pictures, Chicken & Egg Films, and The New York Times HIghlights From Points North Forum (sponsored by ESPN Films): — Memory Work: Activating Black Archives creates a dialogue between two CIFF selections, Once Upon a Time in Harlem and Windows of Time , and Harvard Black Film Project’s Jackie Glover exploring the significance of community-driven archival practices in the context of the federal government’s erasure and revision of Black histories. —Three sessions take up the current state of public media: *In Field Briefing: Public Interest Media at Risk , Maggie Bowman presents the findings of a new report commissioned by the Ford Foundation, which documents approximately $45 million in direct federal investment in public-interest documentary eliminated by the cuts of 2025. *In Public Media Metamorphosis, executives from FRONTLINE , American Documentary , WXXI and NPR Studios describe how their organizations are expanding into digital distribution as the traditional broadcast model is disrupted. *The Forum closes on Sunday with a regional strategy session convened with Future Film Coalition and the Maine Film Association , asking what it would take to build a more durable media ecosystem in New England. —Magnum photographer Alessandra Sanguinetti , director of the CIFF opener and Locarno winning The Illusion of an Everlasting Summer , will discuss her artistic practice with Cinema Tropical’s Carlos A. Gutiérrez . —Festival alum Keith Wilson brings the fourth episode of Pleased to Announce , his live documentary performance on the financial and emotional costs of awards campaigns, following presentations at CPH:DOX, Cannes and DC/DOX. —Finally, the 5th edition of Points North’s Documentary Town Hall , moderated by Beadie Finzi , will explore how documentary filmmakers and their allies can respond to this moment of uncertainty with vision, ambition and deeper collaboration, building new models for connecting independent work with audiences. Further details about 2026 Points North Institute Artist Programs : Points North Fellowship The Points North Fellowship supports six filmmaking teams as they develop their pitches and publicly present their documentary features-in-progress to a panel of funders and distributors at CIFF’s popular Points North Pitch. Points North’s Executive Director, Elise McCave , will moderate the event. Confirmed pitch panelists include Andrea Alarcón , Sundance Institute; Opal H. Bennett , American Documentary | POV; Daniel J. Chalfen , Naked Edge Films; Nikki Heyman, Doc Society; Eric Hynes , Jacob Burns Film Center; Kiyoko McCrae , Chicken & EggFilms; Anya Rous, Multitude Films; and Paulina Suarez, Ford Foundation. The program’s mentors are Assia Boundaoui , Kristin Feeley, and Andrea Meditch . The program is made possible by sponsorship from the deNovo Initiative. Points North Fellowship Projects Choreography of a Tyrant (France, Syria, USA, Norway, Qatar) Directed by Qutaiba Barhamji. Produced by Anne-Catherine Witt and co-produced by Nesa Azimi. After discovering 14 censored frames showing Hafez al-Assad chasing a fly, a filmmaker investigates how authoritarian power constructs sacred images and how a single flaw can unravel a carefully engineered myth. Hen House (USA) Directed by Julia Rosenheim. Produced by Karen Gaytán & Jazz Szympruch. In Springdale, Arkansas, immigrant poultry workers endure dangerous conditions in silence—until an organizer invites them to turn their experiences into theater. As performing begins to transform how they see themselves, immigration crackdowns force them to decide whether they can afford to keep going. Kamnop: A Treasure is Waiting for You (USA, France, Cambodia, Spain) Directed by Kanitha Heng Snow & Guillermo Roques. Produced by Christian Popp. Kamnop is an exhilarating and transformative road trip, where a mother and daughter travel from Colorado to Cambodia in search of a long-lost treasure, buried during the first days of the Khmer Rouge genocide. Oh Heart, Don’t Be Afraid (Georgia, France, Germany) Directed and produced by Ana Kvichidze. Produced by Mariam Bitsadze, Valerianne Boue and Natalia Imaz. Dachi is a queer person (they/them) from a religious place in Georgia, oppressed by the Archbishop, religious society and even their own family. They find an old witch, taught and empowered with her magic spells and they begin to change reality. Shape of Silence (Canada) Directed and produced by Varun Trikha. Amid changing forests, a blind Polish linguist searches for sounds she believes can express what human language cannot. Untitled Alamo Reenactment Project (USA) Directed by César Martínez Barba. Produced by Henry Kinder & Sean Weiner. Untitled Alamo Reenactment Project explores the construction of the Alamo story. From the voices of reenactors to the ghostly presence of Mexican “soldados” haunting San Antonio, the hybrid film examines how this narrative shapes the landscape of today. 4th World Media Lab Now in its eleventh year, the 4th World Media Lab continues to serve as a vital space for emerging and mid-career Indigenous filmmakers to develop their craft, strengthen their networks and advance projects rooted in cultural integrity and community care. This year’s cohort gathers five visionary artists from across Turtle Island and Pasifika, whose work reflects both artistic rigor and deep relational accountability. The program’s mentors include Yvonne Russo , Tracy Rector , Chris Newell and guest artist Paige Bethmann. The 4th World Media Lab Fellows Noelani Kanuha Auguston is a member of Shx ̌ whá:y Village, with Nooksack and Hawaiian heritage. A wife and mother of two young boys, she and her husband are raising their family in their homelands along the Nooksack River. She earned her BA from the University of Washington and, guided by a deep love of storytelling, went on to earn her MFA in creative writing with a focus in screenwriting from the Institute of American Indian Arts. Noelani currently writes and produces for Children of the Setting Sun Productions. Her work is rooted in an authentic Indigenous worldview, with a particular focus on the peoples of the Salish Sea. She is driven by a commitment to creating hopeful, transformative representations of Native life, especially for youth, offering characters and stories that reflect strength, possibility and self-recognition. Quannah ChasingHorse is a Han Gwich’in and Sicangu/Oglala Lakota land protector and fashion model from Eagle Village, Alaska, and the tribes of South Dakota. Quannah is a fourth-generation land protector; her deep connection to her homelands and her people’s way of life is her grounding and guiding force. She gained prominence through a 2020 Calvin Klein campaign and has since worked with the top global fashion houses; won countless awards; starred in Reservation Dogs and Thin Places ; and graced the covers of numerous magazines, including Vogue , Elle and Harper’s Bazaar . Quannah’s short film, Walking Two Worlds , won awards and streams on The North Face’s channels. Amid Quannah’s accomplishments, her most important work is using her platform to uphold and uplift her Indigenous values and peoples. Montana Cypress is a Los Angeles-based playwright, filmmaker and actor. Originally from the Miccosukee Tribe located in South Florida, he has studied acting at New York Film Academy, the British Academy of Dramatic Acting, and UCLA’s Professional Acting Program. He is a three-time winner of the Von Marie Atchley Excellence in Playwriting Award; winner of Best Native American Directed Short at Phoenix Film Festival; had a full-length comedy stageplay, AChristmas In Ochopee , premiere in Minneapolis, produced by New Native Theatre; and his documentary about alligator wrestling, The Art of Gator Wrestling , can be viewed on PBS North’s YouTube channel. Montana recently played Chief Bromden in the stage adaptation of One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest at the Gainesville Playhouse. He can also be seen in the film Young Washington , released in theaters in July 2026. Banchi Hanuse works across film and radio as a co-founder of Nuxalk Radio, supporting Nuxalk language revitalization, upholding Nuxalk Nationhood and advocating for stewardship of Nuxalk homelands. She directed her first feature documentary, Aitamaako’tamisskapi Natosi: Before the Sun , in 2023. Most recently, Banchi premiered her second feature film, Ceremony , at SXSW in 2026, where it garnered the Documentary Spotlight Audience Award. Lokotah Sanborn is an interdisciplinary artist and filmmaker from the Penobscot Nation Reservation. Lokotah works for Sunlight Media Collective, documenting stories at the intersection of Wabanaki sovereignty and environmental justice. From 2023-25, his video work featured in the traveling exhibition Exploding Native Inevitable , which toured the U.S. He received the Lunder Institute Fellowship (Colby College) and North Star Fellowship (Points North Institute) in 2024 and the David C. Driskell Fellowship (Indigo Arts Alliance) in 2025. His directorial debut, Otherworld , made in collaboration with Odanak Abenaki writer and composer Mali Obomsawin, premiered at BlackStar in August 2025. He co-directed the short Wabanaki Voices in Recovery with Mi’kmaq filmmaker Jared Lank, produced by Points North Institute. His artwork was featured in the MET’s unsanctioned exhibition Encoded , and he won two 2025 Webby Awards. Lokotah is developing his first feature-length documentary. LEF/CIFF Fellowship Points North’s long-standing commitment to supporting regional filmmakers is evident in theLEF/CIFF Fellowship. This program, developed in partnership with the LEF Foundation, offers five New England–based filmmakers with feature documentaries in production or post-production the opportunity to attend CIFF for project development workshops and industry meetings. The LEF/CIFF Fellowship cohort will be mentored by filmmaker Todd Chandler. LEF/CIFF Projects Ancestral Days (USA, Italy) Directed by Bronte Stahl. Produced by Isabella Rinaldi. Francesco leads personalized ancestral tours in Sicily for Americans in search of their roots. Among the bureaucratic, parochial, pastoral and familial spaces his work takes his clients, a reflection on roots, gentrification and the act of remaining emerges. Feu de Lune (Côte d’Ivoire) Directed by Dominic Yarabe. Produced by Eliza Soros, Natalia Almada, Pamela Martinez and Carlo Nasisse. Bobia, a rural village in Côte d’Ivoire, keeps a buried secret. The war has one memory, and it is three generations long. In a place where history was never written down, the memory of this largely erased civil war survives through children’s dreams, adult silences and a mother’s nightly bedtime stories. Patrimony (USA) Directed by Musa Syeed. Produced by Razi Jafri. Dr. Syeed is a retired leader of the Muslim community, a diehard optimist and, at 80, he’s losing his memory and his voice. He’s desperate to find someone to document his eventful life, from serving time as a political prisoner in Kashmir to his pioneering interfaith work in America. But the best he can find is a reluctant, cynical filmmaker who happens to be his youngest son: me. Someone’s Father (USA, Colombia) Directed by Andrea Patiño Contreras. Produced by Gabriela Díaz Arp. Amidst her father’s terminal cancer, a filmmaker interrogates the origins of a family heirloom: a tsantsa, or shrunken human head, acquired by her grandfather in the 1940s. As her father reckons with the question of where to rest his own body, the filmmaker wonders whether the tsantsa deserves the same. Topology of a House (Hong Kong) Directed by Kai Luo. Produced by Sol Ye. After the property crisis cuts off family support, a filmmaker returns from the US to find his home demolished by a bankrupt father who once shaped Shenzhen’s skyline. Drifting in a city in economic retreat, he searches for the meaning of making a family film amid the family’s collapse. Diane Weyermann Fellowship The Diane Weyermann Fellowship at Points North was established to honor the legacy of Diane Weyermann , a prolific producer and pillar of the nonfiction filmmaking community. The Fellowship identifies three advanced career directors and producers working on creatively expansive, cinematic feature-length documentaries that address poignant and urgent themes of our time. The 18-month program is one of the most robust artist development initiatives for documentary filmmakers offered by a U.S.-based organization. The Diane Weyermann Fellowshipprovides $100,000 in unrestricted funding for each project, as well as two creative retreats. The program is tailored to the needs of each film team, giving each project team a creative space to explore and expand possibilities for their films and careers. The Diane Weyermann Fellowship was developed by Points North in partnership with Participant Media and is made possible by seed funding from the Skoll Foundation and major support from the RandomGood Foundation , Ford Foundation’s JustFilms and over 200 individual supporters. The cohort will be joined on their final retreat by creative advisors Kirsten Johnson, Andrea Meditch and Tabitha Jackson . The 2025-2026 Weyermann Fellowship projects and artists follow: Captions Will Be Needed (USA, Mexico) Directed by Natalia Almada. Produced by Esther Robinson and Josh Penn. Captions Will be Needed is filmmaker Natalia Almada’s cinematic response to living with a rare cancer that has reconfigured her relationship to time. Testimony (Australia) Directed and produced by Maya Newell. Produced by Alex Kelly, Larissa Behrendt AO, Sophie Hyde and Lisa Sherrard. As the climate emergency rises before them, Torres Strait Islanders too rise up, suing the government for failing to prevent climate harm. While the court can only hold part of the story, we dance, remember and dream of possible futures with Saibai and her people. This film is their testimony. The Instrument (USA) Directed by Zac Manuel. Produced by Darcy McKinnon. An aging jazz singer sets out with his filmmaker son to use artificial intelligence to resurrect the voice of his late father. title: Barunson E&A Boards ‘Satan’s Slaves: Origin’; Franchise Prequel Billed As Joko Anwar’s Most Ambitious Production
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Rashaana Shah & Manasi Parekh Join $10M AIF Media Fund; Initial Slate Headed By Rick Moody Adaptation ‘Purple America’ Lionsgate Strikes Promotional Partnership With Indian Action Star Yash Google DeepMind, Kling AI & Alibaba Join Busan Market’s InnoAsia 2026 Program View All August 31, 2026 8:00am Satan's Slaves: Origin Rapi Films Barunson E&A, the Korean studio behind Bong Joon Ho’s Oscar-winning Parasite , has boarded worldwide sales on Satan’s Slaves: Origin , the latest addition to the blockbuster horror franchise directed by Indonesian filmmaker Joko Anwar . The company will launch the project, which it is billing as “one of the most ambitious genre productions to come out of Southeast Asia”, to international buyers at the inaugural TIFF Market this September. Written and directed by Anwar, Satan’s Slaves: Origin is produced by Rapi Films, in co-production with Anwar’s Come and See Pictures, Sky Media and Legacy Pictures. Related Stories News TrustNordisk Unveils Fresh Deals & Teaser Trailer For Venice Contender 'Woman Unknown' News Alma Har'el's Family Drama 'Wet' Heading To TIFF Market With 193; A-List Cast Circling The film is currently in pre-production and targeting a 2027 theatrical release in Indonesia. Watch on Deadline It marks Anwar’s most ambitious production to date, unfolding across two continents and told in seven languages including Indonesian, Alsatian, Portuguese, Javanese, Dutch, Turkish and Latin. Anwar’s reboot of Rapi Films’ 1980 Indonesian cult classic of the same name started in 2017 with Satan’s Slaves , which became Indonesia’s highest-grossing local film of the year and kickstarted the country’s horror boom. Its sequel, Satan’s Slaves: Communion , became the first Indonesian feature released in IMAX and ranks among the top six highest-grossing local films of all time in Indonesia. The third installment in the franchise, Satan’s Slaves: Origin , is built as a standalone prequel, tracing the origins of the cult and demonic pact that set the first two films in motion. It begins with a mysterious mass hysteria gripping 16th-century Strasbourg – inspired by a real-life incident in 1518 – before arriving at a haunted lighthouse on the southern coast of 17th-century Java, expanding the mythology beyond anything the franchise has attempted before. Anwar also recently directed horror comedy Ghost In The Cell , which premiered at Berlin film festival and is currently the second highest-grossing film of the year at Indonesia’s box office with more than 3.3 million admissions. The film, which is also part of Anwar and Barunson E&A’s two-year exclusive partnership, has been sold to 150 territories worldwide, including Plaion for German rights and Well Go USA for North America. Commenting on Satan’s Slaves: Origins , Anwar said: “This film is everything I didn’t know I was building toward – the one that finally answers where the curse came from, why it never stopped, and what it’s really after. Longtime fans are going to get the answers they’ve waited years for. Newcomers are going to get the ride of their lives.” Yoonhee Choi, CEO of Barunson E&A, said: “Every time we work with Joko Anwar, the scale gets bigger and the ambition gets sharper. Satan’s Slaves: Origin is unlike anything he’s made – a story that moves across centuries and continents. It’s proof of what we’ve believed for years: Indonesian filmmakers are telling some of the boldest genre stories in the world right now, and we’re proud to help this one reach it.” Barunson E&A’s pan-Asian slate also includes Thai horror Inherit from Banjong Pisanthanakun, produced by Thailand’s GDH 559 and selected for this year’s Toronto International Film Festival; Indonesian zombie-apocalypse blockbuster Zona Merah: Dead City ; and Korean occult mystery Stoneborn , from the team behind Exhuma . full_text: Aug 31, 2026 7:44am PT Dolly Parton Estate Sets Two-Day DollyFests for Nashville and London in 2027, Says These ‘Parties of a Lifetime’ Will Take the Place of a Public Memorial By Chris Willman Plus Icon Chris Willman Senior Music Writer and Chief Music Critic ChrisWillman Latest Dolly Parton Estate Sets Two-Day DollyFests for Nashville and London in 2027, Says These ‘Parties of a Lifetime’ Will Take the Place of a Public Memorial 2 hours ago At Daisy Chain Fields, Olivia Rodrigo, Chappell Roan and Honored Forebears Convene for a Superb Festival That’s Hot to Go in Every Way: Concert Review 23 hours ago Sara Bareilles Sings About Loss — and It’s Our Gain — in the Beautifully Bittersweet ‘Good Grief’: Album Review 3 days ago See All The Dolly Parton estate has announced the first large public programs honoring the life and music of the late superstar, with events titled “DollyFest: The Celebration of a Lifetime” set to take place in Nashville and London on successive weekends in 2027. Dates have not yet been announced for the two-day festivals. The estate said that a DollyFest had already been planned for Nashville in January 2027, with the artist’s participation, and now will go on in her memory, with the addition of a separate London event. Related Stories San Sebastián Co-Production Forum: Celina Murga, Mariana Rondón, Matias Mariani, Santiago Loza and Christopher Murray Among Selected Naomi Watts to Be Honored at San Sebastián Film Festival This may be the closest that Parton fans get to a public memorial, as Danny Nozell, her longtime business partner and founder/CEO of CTK Enterprises, noted in a statement that “as far as a traditional memorial goes, that is not something Dolly wanted.” Popular on Variety An announcement for the festivals says that “what was originally planned as a multi-artist event for January 2026 in Nashville and intended to feature Parton as performer and host will now morph into a global double-day, double-weekend, double-continent party of a lifetime.” Nozell said that the original plan had been to hold an event on her birthday this past Jan. 19. “What Dolly started, we will ensure is brought to life. Many people behind the scenes know that DollyFest is a dream of Dolly’s that was intended to take place on her 80th birthday in Nashville. We had the venue booked and we had the announcement ready to go. And then, in August 2025, Dolly had to take a step back after her initial health challenges. A lot of people always say, WWDD (What Would Dolly Do?), and, well, at this moment, DollyFest is WDWD (What Dolly Would Do!).” Nozell suggested that the estate will not stand in the way of the many Parton tributes and memorials that are inevitable for this fall, but that this represents the estate’s official commemoration of her life, believing that she would want to be remembered via a festival more than any more solemn public occasion. “We are not discouraging people from celebrating Dolly in the ways they choose,” he said. “However, as far as a traditional memorial goes, that is not something Dolly wanted. title: Isabelle Huppert Vampire Film ‘The Blood Countess’ Bought for North America (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Aug 31, 2026 7:36am PT Isabelle Huppert Vampire Film ‘The Blood Countess’ Bought for North America (EXCLUSIVE) Strand Releasing has acquired 'The Blood Countess' for North America, ahead of its U.S. premiere at Fantastic Fest. By Elsa Keslassy Plus Icon Elsa Keslassy International Correspondent @elsakeslassy Latest Isabelle Huppert Vampire Film ‘The Blood Countess’ Bought for North America (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Venice Film Festival Maintains Jury Press Conference After Solving ‘Scheduling Issues’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago ‘Bunker’ Director Florian Zeller on Casting Real-Life Couple Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem for His Marriage-in-Crisis Drama 4 days ago See All Courtesy of Amour Fou Vienna, Amour Fou Luxembourg, Heimatfilm/P. Domenigg Strand Releasing has acquired North American rights to Ulrike Ottinger’s “The Blood Countess,” the baroque black comedy starring Isabelle Huppert as the legendary Countess Elizabeth Báthory. The film, which world premiered in the Berlinale Special Gala section earlier this year, will make its U.S. premiere at Fantastic Fest on Sept. 17. Strand is planning a theatrical release in spring 2027. Related Stories San Sebastian Adds Jesse Eisenberg, Fred Cavayé, Amanda Kernell Films to Golden Shell Race San Sebastián Sets Michaël R. Roskam’s ‘Le Faux Soir’ as Closing Night Film The deal was negotiated by Jon Gerrans on behalf of Strand Releasing and Magnify Film Sales. Popular on Variety “We’re thrilled to be handling this unique film from Ms. Ottinger and look forward to working with Isabelle again on another film,” said Marcus Hu of Strand Releasing. Strand has previously released several films starring Huppert, including Catherine Breillat’s “Abuse of Weakness,” Michael Haneke’s “Time of the Wolf” and Guillaume Nicloux’s “Valley of Love.” Inspired by the life and mythology surrounding Báthory, the 16th-century Hungarian aristocrat who became notorious in folklore as a serial killer, “ The Blood Countess ” sees Huppert’s character awaken from a centuries-long slumber and set out across Vienna with her devoted maid Hermine in search of a mysterious book capable of destroying her. The film was written by Ottinger with Elfriede Jelinek, the Nobel Prize-winning Austrian author of “The Piano Teacher,” and marks the culmination of a project the German filmmaker first conceived more than 25 years ago. “I wrote the screenplay in 1998, in the last century, which sounds crazy now,” Ottinger told Variety ahead of the film’s Berlinale premiere, adding that she had wanted to make the project “for a very long time.” Ottinger, a leading figure of German avant-garde cinema whose films include “Madame X — An Absolute Ruler,” “Ticket of No Return” and “Freak Orlando,” said Huppert had been attached in spirit almost from the outset. Rather than approaching Báthory through conventional psychological realism, Ottinger conceived Huppert’s vampire as an imperious, almost mythic presence. “Here, the countess is iconic,” Ottinger said. “She is despotic and completely in control of her surroundings,” adding that Huppert “brought glamour and elegance to that authority.” Ottinger, who received the Berlinale’s Honorary Golden Bear in 2020, also used elaborate costumes, production design and a highly stylized vision of Vienna to playfully subvert vampire-movie conventions. The cast is completed by Birgit Minichmayr, Lars Eidinger, Thomas Schubert, André Jung and Tom Neuwirth, better known as Conchita Wurst. Strand Releasing currently has Brydie O’Connor’s “Barbara Forever” and Gregg Araki’s 4K restoration of “Mysterious Skin” in release. Its upcoming slate also includes Mexico’s Oscar entry “On the Road,” directed by David Pablos. title: Randy Quaid Slams Tom Cruise Over Anne Hathaway ‘Days of Thunder 2’ Role: “Anne Isn’t Sexy”

On the heels of Tom Cruise announcing a Days of Thunder sequel — which will return Cruise as NASCAR driver Cole Trickle — Cruise’s former co-star Randy Quaid crudely blasted the action movie icon for picking Oscar winner Anne Hathaway as his co-lead . In the 1990 original, Quaid played a race team owner who recruits Cole into NASCAR, while Nicole Kidman played a neurosurgeon who becomes Cole’s love interest. In the upcoming Paramount movie, Hathaway will play a team owner and engineer. You need the original girl. It’s not personal; it’s filmmaking. Anne isn’t sexy, because and if you haven’t noticed, she’s pregnant.” The actor — who has 1.2 million followers and whose feed is full of MAGA-related content — continued: “If I were in control of production, a real sequel worth watching for DAYS OF THUNDER would be seeing Tom and Nicole together on screen again. We don’t need a new girl; we need a new race car! … Anne Hathaway is a leftist, woke, horrible choice for DAYS OF THUNDER NASCAR audience who are MAGA. The sexy older chick for Tom in this film needs to be Nicole. That’s the casting that would sell the idea. It’s interesting because when we made the first one there was also a rush to get it out; editors slept in the cutting room on shifts. This is a weird thing, like they want it to come out and tank.” Several of Quaid’s followers defended Hathaway, while another noted, “I find it more than a bit performative that you simultaneously argue conservatives in Hollywood should not lose out on work because of their politics but those on the Left should.” Hathaway is fresh off two blockbusters with The Devil Wears Prada 2 and The Odyssey . She next stars in the title role in Verity , based on Colleen Hoover’s bestselling novel. Quaid’s comments came after the actor posting a video suggesting that he would be a part of the sequel. In the video, he’s driving a car and declared, “Tom Cruise just called me! We’re making Days of Thunder 2 !” Paramount had no immediate comment. Jonathan Levine will direct the new Thunder , with Will Staples writing the screenplay. Cruise, Jerry Bruckheimer and Tommy Harper are producing. title: Zack Snyder’s ‘The Last Photograph’ to World Premiere at Toronto Film Festival
full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All August 31, 2026 7:01am 'The Last Photograph' Toronto Film Festival Zack Snyder s going from the epic world of DC superheroes to the Toronto Film Festival with a special event screening for his passion project The Last Photograph. His jungle-set indie will have a first look at TIFF as an acquisition title as no studio and streamer has yet nabbed the rights to the title. The Last Photograph will debut before fest-goers and possibly buyers on Sunday, Sept. 12, in the John Bassett Theater, a theater in the Metro Toronto Convention Centre, the Front Street venue for the festival’s inaugural official content market. Related Stories Movies In 'Love Is the Monster,' Paulina García Is a Granny Facing Impossible Choices (Exclusive TIFF Trailer) Movies 'Pokémon: Wild Card' Movie Announced for 2027; Teaser Released The long-in-the-works picture from Snyder sidesteps the zombies, superheroes and starships that made him one of Hollywood’s biggest filmmakers. Starring Stuart Martin and Fra Free, The Last Photograph follows an ex-DEA agent seeking revenge in a South American jungle where dangerous terrain and inner demons combine for drama. A 2025 synopsis from the producers issued as production got underway described Snyder’s film as: “An ex-DEA operative must return to the mountains of South America in an effort to find his missing niece and nephew, following the brutal murders of their diplomat parents. Enlisting the help of a washed-up junkie war photographer, the only person to have seen the face of the killers, he sets out, determined to find the children and the truth, but soon learns he must also face the ghosts of his past. Their journey into the unknown takes them further and further away from civilization, bringing into question everything they believe, while slowly eroding the distinction between real and surreal.” Both Martin and Free starred in Snyder’s Rebel Moon movies. Snyder originated The Last Photograph based on his own story and had been developing the war drama since the mid-2000s, after the success of 300. In the early 2010s, Christian Bale and Sean Penn were attached to star in the long-in-development project, before Snyder took a detour into his DC movies. Longtime colleague Kurt Johnstad and Snyder wrote the script for The Last Photograph after their work together on 300 and Rebel Moon. THR

title: John Galliano Bows Out, Met Gala Exhibit Canceled Amid Backlash
full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All August 31, 2026 6:24am John Galliano Kevin Tachman/MG19/Getty Images for The Met Museum/Vogue John Galliano has bowed out of the Met Gala where he was set to be honored amid growing backlash over past remarks by the veteran designer, including an antisemitic rant. “After much reflection and discussion with all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time,” Galliano said Monday in an Instagram post. “Following thoughtful discussions with John Galliano, we have together decided not to proceed with the exhibition,” The Metropolitan Museum of Art’s director and chief executive officer Max Hollein said in a statement on Monday morning. Related Stories Lifestyle Met Gala Organizers Reportedly Mulling Date Change Amid John Galliano Backlash Lifestyle Fashion Keeps Debating John Galliano. It's Ignoring Its Jewish History. The annual, star-studded exhibit, John Galliano: Horizons , had been set for May 3, and was bring overseen by Anna Wintour , Vogue’s global editorial director who also serves as a Met trustee. But outrage over plans to honor Galliano, who is credited with growing luxury-fashion brand Dior into a global giant, left Met Gala organizers in damage control. Met Gala organizers will make announcements on a new spring Costume Institute exhibition and the overall 2027 edition at a later date. “I do not want the debate surrounding me to place the Met in a difficult position or to distract from the remarkable work of the Costume Institute. I also recognize and respect that the exhibition honoring my work would be painful for some,” Galliano added in his statement. Wintour said in a statement in support of Galliano as he headed for the exit: “John’s decision that the exhibition devoted to his work should not take place at this time is very courageous and a measure of the man he is. I believe this is the right decision, and both he and the Museum have my full support.” Andrew Bolton, curator of The Met’s Costume Institute, in his own statement said, “I believe deeply in the responsibility of museums to examine difficult histories with rigor, candor, and care. I also recognize the pain and concern this exhibition has caused. After extensive discussion, I support the decision not to proceed. I remain deeply grateful to my colleagues and to the advisors, lenders, collaborators, and community leaders who contributed their knowledge, trust, and perspectives to the project.” Galliano was fired by Christian Dior in 2011 after video footage surfaced showing the designer, who was inebriated, making antisemitic remarks in a Paris bar, La Perle. French laws at the time made it a crime to incite racial hatred. The chief Dior designer was also arrested for allegedly assaulting two people with antisemitic and racist outbursts that included comments like “I love Hitler,” “People like you would be dead” and “Your mothers, your forefather” would all be “gassed.” His racist remarks were also said to include “fucking ugly Jewish bitch” and “fucking Asian bastard.” After the incident, Galliano retreated from public life for two years and was found guilty by a Paris court of a hate crime for public insults based on religion, race and ethnicity for two incidents in Feb. 2011 and another in Oct. 2010 when a woman claimed he made similar racist outbursts in the same bar near to where he lived. Galliano received a suspended fine of $8,400 and was forced to pay damages and court fees. Galliano met with Jewish leaders and rabbis following the scandal and received blessings from groups like the Anti-Defamation League. In July, the Metropolitan Museum of Art announced that Galliano’s work would be spotlighted in the Met’s Costume Institute. This exhibition, while was to draw on the Met’s extensive collection of Galliano fashion pieces, serves as the centerpiece for the annual Met Gala , an event attended by the most elite of the A-list, with one of the most coveted invites. Galliano’s withdrawal from the planned Met Gala spotlight was preceded on Sunday by a New York Times story that pointed to critics, including donors, politicians and Jewish leaders, having taken aim at the Metropolitan Museum for championing a fashion industry giant after he had been convicted for a hate crime in 2011. The tribute to Galliano would have made him the third living designer to receive a solo exhibition at the Met, following Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo in 2017. The full statement from Galliano is below: I am profoundly grateful to The Metropolitan Museum of Art, and particularly to Max Hollein, Andrew Bolton and Anna Wintour, for the extraordinary honor of proposing an exhibition devoted to my work. To have my creative journey considered by an institution that I have admired throughout my life moved me more deeply that I can express. I will remain forever grateful for the confidence, care and scholarship that Max, Andrew, Anna and the entire Met team brought to this project. After much reflection and discussion with all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time. I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry. I understand that meaningful atonement is not achieved through an exhibition, institutional recognition or a single public gesture. It is a continuing responsibility, demonstrated through listening, learning and one’s conduct over time. I do not want the debate surrounding me to place the Met in a difficult position or to distract from the remarkable work of the Costume Institute. I also recognize and respect that the exhibition honoring my work would be painful for some. I would also like to express my deepest gratitude to all those who have guided, supported and accompanied me throughout those fifteen years of sobriety and recovery from alcoholism and addiction. Your wisdom, patience and humanity have helped me more than I can ever adequately express. I remain profoundly indebted to you for giving me, as you promised, a life better than I could ever have dreamt of. My gratitude to the Met, Max, Andrew and Anna remains profound and enduring. Their generosity, humanity and belief in the importance of fashion as art, culture and history – as well as their understanding of human fragility and the possibility of growth – will remain with me always. John Galliano THR

title: Howard Stern Cuts SiriusXM Show to Once a Week, Inks HBO Max Deal for Streaming
full_text: × Skip to main content By Caitlin Huston Plus Icon Caitlin Huston Business Writer hustonca Follow Sign Up View All August 31, 2026 6:14am Howard Stern Jason Koerner/Getty Images Howard Stern is returning to SiriusXM with one live show a week, plus a new deal with HBO Max. Stern returns to his longtime SiriusXM Sept. 14 and will embark on one new show a week, airing Monday, down from two per week. Additionally, Stern will adapt his live SiriusXM show into a streamable episode for HBO Max, alongside extras. The Howard Stern Show on HBO Max will debut Sept. 17, with episodes released on Thursdays. “There’s simply no one like Howard, and the start of his new season is another exciting chapter in an extraordinary run,” said Scott Greenstein, SiriusXM’s President and Chief Content Officer. “For more than two decades at SiriusXM, he’s continued to evolve, surprise audiences and deliver the kind of conversations and moments that only Howard can. We are proud that Howard chose to continue with SiriusXM through 2028 for his exclusive live show and deep library of classic Howard, and that Howard, HBO Max and SiriusXM have now teamed up to create a compelling new video version of his show.” The news comes after Stern struck a new three year-contract with SiriusXM amid rumors of a retirement, or a show cancellation, which Stern pranked his listeners about by suggesting that Andy Cohen would take over his channel. With the one show a week, Howard Stern’s Howard 101 channel is leaving the SiriusXM lineup, with Stern’s content airing on his remaining channel, Ch. 100. Radio Andy, hosted by Cohen, will move to Ch. 101 from Ch. 102. On Sept. 14, Howard will also unveil a new lineup for his Howard 100 channel, which will include Wrap Up Wednesday , an expanded version of Howard’s Wrap Up Show hosted by Gary Dell’Abate and Jon Hein. The Howard Stern section of the SiriusXM app is also expanding to include Howard Stern Decades for access to Stern’s content from the 80’s, 90’s, 00’s and 10’s. THR

title: Venice Film Festival Changes Course To Reinstate Jury Press Conference: How It Went Down
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman , Melanie Goodfellow August 30, 2026 1:34pm Venice jury 2025 Good news. The Venice Film Festival has reinstated its jury press conference, overturning an unusual move to scrap the traditional opening event this year. The festival responded to Deadline’s inquiry on Sunday by confirming that the press conference was now on. A day earlier, the A-list festival, which kicks off on Wednesday, had told Deadline that the press conference was off due to a scheduling conflict. “The opening conference is not being held due to coinciding commitments,” a senior member of the festival’s press team wrote to Deadline Saturday. The cancellation was also confirmed by a top festival executive who noted to Deadline that, as a “remedy”, there would be a “more relaxed welcome cocktail” with some press instead. Related Stories News Venice Film Festival Scraps Jury Press Conference Festivals Nigeria Has Its First Venice Giornate Entry With Damilola Orimogunje's Family Portrait 'Dear Ajayi' -- First-Look Trailer Deadline’s report (which was flagged to the festival ahead of publication) on the matter triggered backlash, leading to the change of course by the festival. Watch on Deadline Ultimately, this is good news for the press, transparency and all those who rightly want to hear from the jury. What it shouldn’t be is an opportunity for point-scoring or denigrating anyone, least of all the press doing their job. Deadline’s questions to the festival about the jury conference had come about following the conference’s clear omission from the festival schedule, which was highly unusual. We asked multiple times why that was, but didn’t hear back. Until we insisted, and then heard back on Saturday. Maybe there was a scheduling conflict concerning the jury head or a number of jury members. It’s possible. But that would also be highly unusual given that this is a staple commitment of all A-list juries. The context here, as we laid out in our piece yesterday, is that festivals have been desperate to diminish the politically charged nature of press conferences all year. The festival has flatly denied that those were its motivations. This year’s Venice Film Festival international jury is headed by Maggie Gyllenhaal with members comprising Tunisian director and screenwriter Kaouther Ben Hania, the English composer and artist Daniel Blumberg, the Italian professor Francesco Casetti, the French director and screenwriter Xavier Giannoli, the Afghan director and screenwriter Shahrbanoo Sadat, and the Hong Kong director and producer Johnnie To. Jury press conferences have become a minefield for those on stage in recent years as journalists ask questions about their views on global politics, especially the Israel-Gaza war. At last year’s Venice jury press conference, jury head Alexander Payne admitted he was “unprepared” to answer questions about Gaza as political issues dominated. This year’s Berlin Film Festival was a highly charged edition with the opening jury press conference proving to be a flashpoint after jury president Wim Wenders said filmmakers should stay out of politics in answer to a question on the Israel-Palestine conflict. Other thorny topics likely to be on the table this Venice include the dearth of female directors in the main competition, the Iran-U.S. conflict and the Russian-Ukraine War. This festival is already shaping up to include a large dose of politics with the addition of Israel-Gaza doc NAZA and the inclusion of Russian film DAU . Last week, Nobel Prize-winning author Annie Ernaux, Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters and filmmakers including Matteo Garrone and Isabel Coixet were among signatories of an open letter urging the Venice Biennale and film festival to take “concrete action in support of Palestine.” The festival will run September 2 – 12, 2026. Currently, per Rentrak, the North American box office for the first Friday in May through EOD today stands at $4.598 billion , officially the second-highest summer ever behind 2013. If this summer is going to beat 2013’s all-time high, it has $158M to gross. If this week and next Labor Day weekend over performs, no sweat, but the estimation by some sources is that we could come up $18M-$22M short of 2013’s all-time high. title: Your Move, Mr. Governor: CA Post Production Tax Incentive Bill Passes State Senate; Moves To Newsom’s Desk
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Tom Tapp , Dominic Patten August 30, 2026 4:31pm Gavin Newsom Tayfun Coskun/Anadolu via Getty Images State support for the contracting L.A. film and TV industry is now in the hands of California Governor Gavin Newsom and some (hoperfully) very creative accountants. With just hours to spare, the California State Senate passed SB 2319 by a vote of 33-5. The legislation creates a separate tax incentive for the post-production industry. The bill now moves on to Newsom’s desk. Related Stories News California Lawmakers Introduce Compromise For Film Industry On Corporate Tax Credit Cap News Sacramento’s Mad Legislative Dash To Fix Tax Credits SNAFU, Get Post-Production Incentive Passed, Or Not Earlier this year, state representatives talked about the post-production credit reaching up to $100 million in allocated incentives across VFX, scoring, mixing and more. That sky-high number is now more realistically envisioned at around $35 million for the first year. It has one big problem: Should Newsom sign SB 2319, there’s no funding for it. Watch on Deadline Yet, as close as the post-production credit might be to being added to the incentives program administered by the California Film Commission , the reality is there is still no actual funding in place for it. The borderline-baroque $352 billion state budget is so tightly wound with its zero-deficit demands that money for such a new credit is nowhere to be seen, no matter how hard Hollywood has advocated for it and, truth be told, desperately needs it to turn the job losses around. Should Newsom — who has aspirations to the White House — sign the bill, the state’s accounting boffins will have to find a way to fund it. The Motion Picture Editor’s Guild issued a statement praising the bill’s passing. On the corporate side of things, State lawmakers on Friday introduced a bill meant to allow studios a few key exemptions from a recently enacted restriction on corporate tax credits. AB136, introduced Friday evening, addresses concerns raised from stakeholders including the Motion Picture Association about the threat of undermining the efforts to expand California’s Film & TV Tax Credit pool to $750 million. Lawmakers have to consider legislation for 72 hours before voting. With that in mind, a vote on AB136 is likely to come Monday evening, hours before the midnight end to the legislative session. Watch on Deadline Tell a friend to tell a friend pic.twitter.com/2DruSoZSI5 — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 31, 2026 The Rams did not disclose details of his contract, but ESPN and the NFL Network both reported that it was a one-year, $20 million deal with playoff incentives that could raise the total value of the deal to $30 million. He is one of three players in NFL history to have won the Associated Press NFL Defensive Player of the Year Award three times — 2017, 2018 and 2020. If Donald can even approach his previous level of play, his return could give the Rams a devastating pair of pass rushers. The team acquired reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett on June 1. Garrett, 30, set the NFL’s single-season record for sacks last year with 23, and was voted the NFL’s Defensive Player of the Year for the second time. He added a league-leading 33 tackles for loss. According to ESPN, that makes L.A. the only team with two active players who won multiple Defensive Player of the Year awards. The Rams’ Opening Night game this Thursday is against longtime NFC West rivals the San Francisco 49ers on Netflix. Donald could play, but no announcement has yet been made. title: Carlos Reygadas’ Long-Awaited Movie ‘Heil Jupiter!’ Sets Sales With Mk2 Films
full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie TrustNordisk Unveils Fresh Deals & Teaser Trailer For Venice Contender ‘Woman Unknown’ Carlos Reygadas’ Long-Awaited Movie ‘Heil Jupiter!’ Sets Sales With Mk2 Films Venice Film Festival Changes Course To Reinstate Jury Press Conference: How It Went Down View All August 31, 2026 2:45am Heil Jupiter! Carlos Reygadas EXCLUSIVE: Paris-based mk2 films has acquired international sales rights to Carlos Reygadas long-awaited new feature Heil Jupiter! ahead of its world premiere at the New York Film Festival in late September. The radical filmmaker’s first feature since Our Time in 2018, Heil Jupiter! is billed as “a visionary cinematic experience and a nightmarish reflection” on the resistance of love and beauty in our times, no matter how deep the darkness. The official synopsis reads: “Amidst crashing waves and monumental rocks on a distant coast, two young couples open up a realm of shifting realities. Unbeknownst to them, a mysterious entity watches from high above with Godlike judgment. Related Stories News MK2 Films Boards Yuval Abraham & Rachel Szor's Venice Doc 'NAZA' Festivals New York Film Festival Sets Revivals Lineup With Ken Russell's 'The Devils', Powell & Pressburger's 'Gone To Earth' Between these spaces exists a world balanced on the edge of the modern and the primitive, the high-tech and the rural, the corporeal and the mythic. This dreamlike astonishment is a work of feral cinematic expression, splendid in its elemental pleasures, which exist in profound and challenging contrast to its depiction of authoritarian brutality.” Watch on Deadline First announced some eight years ago under the title of Wake of Umbra , Heil Jupiter! has been shot across Poland, Portugal, Sweden, Norway, and Mexico. Giving an update on the project at the Locarno Film Festival last year, Reygadas acknowledged the duration of the production had been long but said the process of making the film had been one of “deep investigation”. Reygadas first broke through in 2002 with debut feature Japón , which garnered a Cannes Caméra d’Or Special Mention. He would go on to win the festival’s Jury Prize for Silent Light in 2007 followed by Best Director for Tenebras Lux in 2012. Our Time premiered in competition in Venice in 2018. Heil Jupiter! is produced by Cristina Velasco for Paloma Negra Films and Carlos Reygadas for No Dream, in co-production with Madants (Poland), Rosa Films (Portugal), Snowglobe (Sweden), Fat City (U.S.), Felix Culpa (U.S.), Board Cadre (Switzerland), Staer (Norway) plus Marco Perego´s Leaf Entertainment (U.S.) and Duende (U.S.). title: TrustNordisk Unveils Fresh Deals & Teaser-Trailer For Venice Contender ‘Woman Unknown’
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie TrustNordisk Unveils Fresh Deals & Teaser Trailer For Venice Contender ‘Woman Unknown’ Carlos Reygadas’ Long-Awaited Movie ‘Heil Jupiter!’ Sets Sales With Mk2 Films Venice Film Festival Changes Course To Reinstate Jury Press Conference: How It Went Down View All August 31, 2026 3:00am EXCLUSIVE: TrustNordisk has unveiled fresh deals and a teaser-trailer for May el-Toukhy ‘s post-World War II Denmark -set psychological drama Woman Unknown ahead of its world premiere in competition at the Venice Film Festival. Adding to a previously announced sale to Italy (Lucky Red), TrustNordisk has also sealed deals to Benelux (September Films), Latin America (California Filmes), Greece (Neo Films) and the Baltics (Estin Film) with more territories on the verge of being signed. Rising Danish actress Mathilde Arcel ( Second Victims ), stars as Marie, a young nanny and housemaid who is on the cusp of marrying her wealthy, older, widowed employer Christian in the immediate aftermath of the end of World War Two. Related Stories Festivals Venice Film Festival Changes Course To Reinstate Jury Press Conference: How It Went Down News Venice Film Festival Scraps Jury Press Conference Amid the jubilation, there is a darker side to the liberation as woman who fraternized with German soldiers are tracked down and publicly shamed. Marie’s secret past threatens to catch up with her, and she is forced to do everything in her power to preserve her new status as lady of the house in post-war anarchy. Arcel is joined in the cast by Carsten Bjørnlund ( The Legacy ) as the austere figure of Christian; Thorbjørn Hedegaard ( Generations ) as a dangerous, obsessive admirer from Marie’s past and Marina Bouras ( The Idiots ), as the household’s all-seeing housekeeper. Danish Egyptian director el-Toukhy is one of just two female directors in the running for the Golden Lion at Venice this year. Woman Unknown is her third feature film after Long Story Short and Queen of Hearts and continues her co-writing collaboration with screenwriter Maren Louise Käehne. “Even before the film has had its international premiere, it has been an amazing ride – this goes both in terms of festivals, but also in terms of having such a strong group of distributors on board at this early stage and several others currently in talks. We can’t wait for the premiere in Venice on Sunday, where we will for sure be even more busy,” said Susan Wendt, Managing Director at TrustNordisk. Following its Venice premiere, Woman Unknown heads to Toronto , where it will make its North American premiere in the Centrepiece sidebar, before playing in competition at the BFI London Film Festival followed by Riga International Film Festival. Woman Unknown is produced Mikael Rieks ( Land of Mine ) for Nordisk Film Production A/S in co-production with Nafta Films, Nordisk Film Production Sweden and Film i Väst. The film received the support of the Danish Film Institute, Eurimages – Council of Europe, Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, Riga City Council, Nordisk Film & TV Fund, DR, The Swedish Film Institute, SVT, LIAA, Riga Film Fund, TrustNordisk and Zentropa. Local distribution is by Nordisk Film Distribution which has set a February 4, 2027 release date in Denmark.
